BLOCKING — OPEN P1 (F21), raised by the PR #325 Copilot review of HEAD 66f1220f, AFTER the 3-cycle plan-review budget was exhausted. DO NOT IMPLEMENT UNTIL DISPOSITIONED BY THE OPERATOR.

DEFECT (verified against the live dependency graph, not inferred): the approval channel is ordered so that the runtime can be completed without ever wiring it in.
* 120.005-T (T16, approvals) depends on 120.004-T (T15, run_session) and 119.004-T.
* 120.005-T has ZERO reverse dependencies — nothing in the program depends on it.
* The runtime chain 120.004-T (T15) -> 120.006-T (T17, CLI adapter) -> 120.007-T (T18, shims) -> 120.008-T (T19, docs) is fully satisfiable with 120.005-T never started.

Yet T15 is specified as THE SINGLE ORCHESTRATOR that composes the session, and plan section 3.6 places the approval exchange inside supervisor runtime behaviour ("the supervisor emits an ApprovalRequested event ... and blocks for the operator's answer"). So T15's acceptance can be met against a run_session() with no approval path, and no later task forces the wiring. The H2 FAIL-CLOSED guarantee — non-interactive approvals resolve to a declared safe default or REFUSED, never silent auto-approval — is a safety control that this ordering permits to be silently omitted from the shipped runtime.

This is the same family as F19 (a shared contract defined downstream of its only consumer), but with a safety consequence rather than only an unimplementable order.

RESOLUTION REQUIRES AN OPERATOR PRODUCT DECISION — Stage records, and does not adopt, because the review budget is spent and the fix is a decomposition change to an already-reviewed plan. Options:
  (A) Split the approval CONTRACT (typed request/response + fail-closed resolution semantics) into a task ordered BEFORE T15, make T15 depend on it, and leave the console rendering implementation downstream of T15; or
  (B) Keep T16 whole but make T15 depend on it and move T15's approval-path integration tests into T15's DoD; or
  (C) Add an explicit wiring obligation to a task that IS on the runtime chain, with a test asserting run_session() routes approvals through approvals.py.

Option (A) matches the resolution direction already recorded for F19, and would let one decomposition change discharge both.

Member of 129-S. 129-S was already gated by F16 and F20; F21 is a third gate on it. Stage adopted no option and changed no dependency edge.

SUPERSEDING RESOLUTION — F21/F32/F33 CLOSED (2026-08-11, Cycle 18 ruling 1, revalidated Cycle 19). The BLOCKING / DO-NOT-IMPLEMENT event above is now DISCHARGED and MUST NOT be read as a live instruction. It was accurate when written and is retained unaltered for audit. THE DEFECT IT DESCRIBED IS FIXED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY ASSERTION: the finding was that this task had ZERO reverse dependencies while depending on the orchestrator, so the supervisor could ship complete without ever importing or invoking approvals.py. The edge is now REVERSED — 120.004-T (T15, run_session, THE SINGLE ORCHESTRATOR) DEPENDS ON this task, and the inverted 120.005-T -> 120.004-T edge was REMOVED. Moving the approval TYPES into contracts.py was explicitly NOT accepted as sufficient, because relocating a type does not make an implementation reachable; the runtime wiring obligation now sits on 120.004-T together with an end-to-end non-interactive test asserting both interactive resolution and non-interactive safe-default/REFUSED behaviour. EVIDENCE (verifier V14, unmodified harness): this task now has at least one REVERSE dependency (120.004-T) where it had ZERO; the orchestrator depends on it; the inverted edge is ABSENT; approvals are TRANSITIVELY REACHABLE from the runtime chain tail 120.008-T, so the chain can no longer complete without them. Full run: verify-plan1-shipment-topology.ps1 221/221 PASS; sim-shipment-closure.ps1 66/66 PASS against engine commit fd8d2c9d. Appended ONLY because the wiring gap is genuinely closed, per the PR #325 reviewer's stated condition.
